notes.title: Nvidia left the rally on read
body: The market bounced Monday. Nvidia went the other way. The weekend group chat had an update. Nvidia’s board opened an independent investigation after reports that someone had targeted CEO Jensen Huang to gather information for a foreign government. The board said it had no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised. The review is still open. That’s the part we actually know.

Now rewind to last week. Stocks rallied right after the midterms. The next day, the Nasdaq fell 5.5% and SOXX, a fund that tracks chip stocks, fell 12.15%. What had people spooked? After Democrats won, investors worried it might get harder to build new data centers. Think permits, power, and local pushback. A GPU can do a lot. It still can’t approve its own power hookup. A delayed build can mean a later shipment.

Here’s where Nvidia gets interesting. It finished last week down 8.8%. Ugly, sure. But the chip fund lost 13.1% over those same five sessions. Nvidia was actually holding up better than the group. On Monday morning the wider market was up and Nvidia was down. A chip selloff can explain why a lot of names fell together last week. It doesn’t get me very far when I’m trying to explain why Nvidia went the other way on Monday. That’s where I’d pay attention to the board news.

So did customers cancel anything? I haven’t seen evidence of that. The board’s statement tells us it’s looking into what happened. It doesn’t say a shipment slipped. The election story has the same problem if you push it too far. Worrying about a permit is one thing. A project actually getting delayed is another. Show me the schedule. I’ll even open the spreadsheet. If the rest of the chip group keeps bouncing while Nvidia lags, I’ll keep a closer eye on Nvidia. If they all start sliding together again, I’ll zoom back out to the broader market.

This is where the boring stuff earns its keep. If customers push back deliveries, I want to know whether Nvidia is sitting on more inventory. If sales keep climbing but customers take longer to pay, I want to see what happened to cash. Those are clues I can check. A rough morning for the stock can tell me investors are nervous. It can’t tell me what’s sitting in a warehouse.

Nvidia reports Nov. 17. I’m watching two things. Does the board find anything that changes how the company operates? And does management say customers are moving delivery dates? Until there’s an answer, I’m keeping last week’s chip selloff and Monday’s Nvidia drop on separate tabs. Yes, I have too many tabs. These two are employed.

performance.window: Five sessions through Nov. 6, 2026 · close to close

notes.flowRemark: Friday’s options trades came before the news. They don’t get credit for seeing Sunday coming. I’m watching who still wants downside protection once the dust settles.
